newsitem.title: CHINA: HK cabinet member sees move on pension plan by May.
newsitem.headline: HK cabinet member sees move on pension plan by May.

text.p: The new Hong Kong government is expected to reach "some conclusion" on a mandatory pension scheme by May 1998, Tam Yiu-chung, a member of the government's Executive Council, said on Thursday.
The so-called Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) would require all employers and employees to contribute five percent of the worker's salary into an authorised annual pension fund.

Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa said on July 1, the first day of the establishment of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) government, that he would step up execution of the Mandatory Provident Fund.
Tam said a two-year study and draft on subsidiary legislation on the MPF has been completed and will be submitted to the Executive Council and then the Provisional Legislature.
Polls to replace the Beijing-installed Provisional Legislature with an elected council are expected to be held in the second quarter of 1998.
Tam said he was not sure when the MPF legislation would be submitted to the Provisional Legislature for assessment, as it has not yet been considered by the Executive Council.
"It takes a long time to scrutinise and assess this subsidiary legislation... I will not be surprised if it takes a few months," he said.
